newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telebras rises on vote.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telebras rises on vote.

text.p: Brazil's Telebras SA rose Thursday, boosted by a congressional vote that helps open Brazils' telecommunication sector to privatization.
State-run Telebras rose 2-1/8 to 147-5/8 in moderate volume. The company's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were among the most active on Wall Street.

The increase followed a vote in the lower house of Brazil's Congress approving a new telecommunications law. The legislation creates a watchdog body that will set rules for the telecoms sector and lay out privatization policy.
"The vote is a very good sign in terms of the likelihood of seeing Brazil create a formal regulator for the sector," said Mickey Schleien, Latin American telecommunications analyst at UBS Securities.
Regulation and privatization policy "are two issues ... that have depressed Telebras' valuation in relation to other Latin American telcos," he said.
Schleien raised his price target for Telebras ADRs to $175 from $145 for the end of the year. The bill goes to the Senate for approval.

Among other active ADRs and foreign shares, Canada's Cineplex Odeon Corp rose 1/8 to 1-7/8 in heavy volume. Daily Variety newspaper reported Thursday that Cineplex Odeon was in merger talks with Sony Theatres, a unit of Japan's Sony Corp.
Swedish telecommunications equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson was off 1/8 to 37-3/8.
Advancers led decliners 232 to 151 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.33 percent in late morning and volume was 19 million ADRs traded. ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
